title: Glucagon-Like Peptide-1 Receptor Agonists for Binge Eating Disorder and Bulimia Nervosa in Children and Adolescents: The Impulsivity Measurement Gap
content: Background: Pediatric prescribing of Glucagon-Like Peptide-1 Receptor Agonists (GLP-1 RA) is expanding faster than the evidence that supports it, with minimal evidence in the treatment of binge-type eating disorders. Impulsivity is central to the binge eating episodes and compensatory behaviors in binge eating disorder (BED) and bulimia nervosa (BN). This scoping review maps GLP-1 RA use in youth with BED and BN, exploring evidence on psychiatric outcomes and impulsivity as a validated outcome measure. Methods: Using JBI methodology and PRISMA-ScR reporting guidelines, we searched across five databases for both peer reviewed literature and data from non-published poster/oral presentations. Studies were imported to JBI SUMARI and evaluated by two independent reviewers, with any conflicts resolved by a third party. Data was extracted, analyzed, and narratively summarized to identify gaps in existing literature. Results: Of 74 identified abstracts, 11 full texts matched inclusion criteria. Included texts were all published/presented between 2021-2025 with notable variation in study design. Some studies demonstrate promise for the use of GLP-1 RA in reducing binge eating behaviors, while others reveal potential for development of restrictive eating. Of the 11 included studies, none used validated measures for impulsivity as post-treatment outcome measure.Conclusions: Although impulsivity is central to binge-eating type pathology and the mechanism behind GLP-1 RA efficacy, there are no studies investigating the therapeutic effect of these drugs on impulsivity. This scoping review highlights areas of high priority for future study concerning the use of GLP-1 RA in pediatric populations with binge-eating type pathology.
